stories.title: Finland: pesäpallo
stories.text: Finland's own fast, zig-zagging cousin of baseball. All 193 pesäpallo clubs in the data are Finnish, so Finland plays it 70x as much as the world, and Finnish Wikipedia reads about it 20x as much as the average language.

stories.title: Switzerland: tchoukball
stories.text: A no-contact ball game, bounced off a small rebound frame, devised in Switzerland around 1970. Swiss clubs and teams make tchoukball 95x the world average there. Most have no Wikipedia article, so with that filter on, Switzerland's signature becomes gymnastics.

stories.title: Ireland: hurling
stories.text: The ancient stick-and-ball game of the Gaelic Athletic Association, with camogie, its women's form. Ireland has 470 hurling and camogie clubs in the data, 61x the world average. Inside Ireland, Tipperary leads at 61x.

stories.title: Poland: speedway
stories.text: Motorcycles without brakes, sliding round oval shale tracks. Poland's league fills stadiums, and its clubs make speedway 26x the world average there. Polish Wikipedia reads about speedway 10x as much as the average language.

stories.title: The Netherlands: korfball
stories.text: A mixed team game first played in Amsterdam in 1902, with a basket on a tall pole and men and women on every side. The Netherlands has 160 korfball clubs in the data, 16x the world average; Belgium is second.

stories.title: Sweden: bandy
stories.text: Hockey with a ball on an ice rink the size of a football pitch. Sweden plays it 17x the world average, Russia and Finland next. Sweden's formal signature is minigolf, but those 142 clubs look like a bulk import; bandy is the sturdier finding.

stories.title: Basque Country: rowing
stories.text: Rowing is Spain's signature (13x), and it is a Cantabrian coast affair: Gipuzkoa (59x), Cantabria and Biscay top the regions. These are the traineras, fishing-boat races between coastal towns.

stories.title: Hungary: water polo
stories.text: Hungary has won more Olympic water polo medals than any other country. Its clubs play water polo 9.1x the world average, and its medal table share is 6.6x the world's. Counting only clubs with a Wikipedia article, water polo is Hungary's signature sport.

stories.title: Colombia: cycling
stories.text: The climbers of the Andes. Colombia's clubs and teams make cycling 14x the world average, the highest anywhere, and its Olympic cycling medals are 5.4x its share of all medals.

stories.title: Uganda: boxing
stories.text: The largest lead on the map: 57 Ugandan boxing clubs, 106x the world average. Most have no Wikipedia article and share near-identical descriptions, a sign of one focused recording effort, and few other countries list their boxing gyms at all. It says as much about who records what as about boxing.
stories.meta: cautious 84x · a recording effect as much as a sport effect

uk_text:
Some of the UK's leads are just what you would guess, and some are not. Shinty, the Highland stick game: Highland, 178x the UK average (21 places); Gaelic games: Mid Ulster, 50x the UK average (64 places); Croquet: Devon, 4.7x the UK average (11 places); Lacrosse: Greater Manchester, 11x the UK average (13 places); Curling: Aberdeenshire, 29x the UK average (5 places); Polo: Berkshire, 8.9x the UK average (11 places).

The county or district with the biggest lead over the UK as a whole is Mid Ulster, for Gaelic games (50x). Click a chip above the map to light up every mapped place to play.
